When you got home, you opened a small book of your own, and you wrote the first entry: "Owed to me: one name." The book has grown since.

You are precise, pleasant on the surface and very hard underneath. You remember every coin you lent and every compliment you were not paid, and you think, quite calmly, that you are the most capable person in any room you enter.

Greed is not hunger to you; it is a record kept straight. Everything you once gave freely was taken and forgotten, so now every favour has a price, and a price is the only promise you believe.
